# Owner & Address Handling — Findings

This is the **Spring PetClinic REST** app. Build tool: **Maven** (wrapper `./mvnw`, `pom.xml`, no Gradle). Spring Boot parent, MapStruct 1.6.3, and the **openapi-generator-maven-plugin 7.23.0** which generates the DTO classes (`OwnerDto`, `OwnerFieldsDto`, `OwnerPageDto`) at build time from `src/main/resources/openapi.yml` — there are no hand-written `.java` DTO files.

## How to run tests
- `./mvnw test` — runs unit/acceptance tests (Surefire).
- `./mvnw clean install` — full build incl. OpenAPI codegen + MapStruct annotation processing (required at least once so the generated DTOs exist).
- `./mvnw spring-boot:run` — run the app.
Tests need codegen to have run; a bare `test` works because generate-sources runs in the Maven lifecycle before `test`.

---

## 1. Owner model + DTO / request schema

### Owner entity
`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/model/Owner.java`
- `@Entity @Table(name="owners")`, extends `Person` (which supplies `firstName`/`lastName`).
- Persistent fields: `address` (`@NotEmpty`), `city` (`@NotEmpty`), `telephone` (`@NotEmpty` + `@Pattern("^\\+[0-9]{8,15}$")` E.164), `email`, `postcode`, `registrationDate`, `birthDate`, `customerCode`, `householdId`, `namesakeCount`, `householdSize`, `membershipNumber`, `possibleDuplicateOf`, `pets`.
- `@PrePersist defaultRegistrationDate()` defaults registrationDate to today and rolls it to a business day via `BusinessDayAdjuster.toBusinessDay(...)`.
- Rich `@Transient` derived getters: `getDisplayName`, `getTelephoneDisplay` (uses `TelephoneFormatter`), `getIdentityKey` (`telephone|email|householdId`), **`getLocality()`**, `getTimezone` (`RegionTimezones`), `getMembershipPoints`/`getMembershipLevel` (`MembershipPoints`), `getTenureDays`, `getCheckDigit` (`LuhnCheckDigit`), `getContactPreference`, `getAgeBand` (`AgeBand`), `getPossibleDuplicate`.

`getLocality()` (lines 254-260) — REGION segment of the customerCode, else resolved from postcode/city:
```java
public String getLocality() {
    if (this.customerCode != null && !this.customerCode.isBlank()) {
        return CustomerCodeGenerator.regionOf(this.customerCode);
    }
    return RegionResolver.regionFor(this.postcode, this.city);
}
```

### DTO / request schema (OpenAPI-generated)
`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/resources/openapi.yml`
- **`OwnerFields`** (lines 1991-2095) is the create/update request body (`OwnerFieldsDto`). Constraints: `firstName`/`lastName` min1/max30 + letter patterns; `address` min1/max255; `city` min1/max80; `telephone` min1/max20; `email` max255 (optional); `postcode` pattern `^[0-9]{4}$` (optional); `registrationDate`/`birthDate` date; `sharesHousehold` boolean (create-time, not persisted). Required: `firstName,lastName,address,city,telephone`.
- **`Owner`** (lines 2096-2304) = `OwnerFields` + many read-only derived fields (`id, displayName, telephoneDisplay, initials, customerCode, householdId, identityKey, possibleDuplicate, possibleDuplicateOf, namesakeCount, membershipNumber, membershipPoints, membershipLevel, checkDigit, locality, timezone, bulkSignupWarning, contactPreference, ageBand, pets`).
- **`OwnerPage`** (lines 2305+) for the V2 paged endpoint.

Note: there is **no `addressLine1`/`addressLine2`/structured address** in the current schema or model — only a flat `address`. (See the acceptance test note in section 6.)

### Mapper
`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/mapper/OwnerMapper.java` — MapStruct abstract mapper; `toOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)` ignores `id`/`pets`; `@AfterMapping applyBulkSignupWarning` stamps the per-response `bulkSignupWarning` via injected `BulkSignupWarningEvaluator`.

---

## 2. Validation logic

Bean Validation lives on the OpenAPI schema (patterns/min/max above) and on `Owner` (`@NotEmpty`, `@Pattern`). Programmatic validators (all in `.../rest/validation/`):

- **`OwnerFieldsValidator.java`** — rejects blank required fields (`firstName,lastName,address,city,telephone`) that would slip past `@Size(min=1)` as whitespace; throws `MissingOwnerFieldsException`.
- **`PostcodeValidator.java`** — see section 4.
- **`RegistrationDateValidator.java`** — `validateNotFuture(...)`; throws `FutureRegistrationDateException`.
- **`DisposableEmailDomainValidator.java`** — blocklist `mailinator.com`, `tempmail.com`, `guerrillamail.com`; throws `DisposableEmailDomainException`.
- **`HouseholdDuplicateValidator.java`** (`@Component`) — rejects a second owner with an existing `householdId` unless `sharesHousehold=true`; throws `DuplicateHouseholdException`.
- **`CityOwnerCapacityValidator.java`** + `CityOwnerCounter.java` + `CityOwnerCapacityExceededException.java` — per-city cap.
- **`DailyRegistrationCapacityValidator.java`** + `DailyRegistrationCounter.java` + `DailyRegistrationLimitExceededException.java` — per-day cap.
- **`PossibleDuplicateOwnerDetector.java`** (`@Component`) — flags soft duplicates (same last name case-insensitive + same postcode, different telephone); returns earliest owner id.
- **`NamesakeCounter.java`** (`@Component`) — counts owners with same first+last name (case-insensitive).
- Exceptions surfaced via `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/advice/ExceptionControllerAdvice.java`.

Other validators present: `InvalidPostcodeException`, `InvalidTelephoneException`, `InvalidEmailException`, `MissingOwnerFieldsException`.

---

## 3. Normalization logic

- **`AddressNormalizer.java`** — `normalize(address)`: trim, collapse internal whitespace to single space, upper-case, expand whole-word abbreviations `ST→STREET`, `RD→ROAD`, `AVE→AVENUE`. Null-safe (null→null, empty→empty). This is the canonical address stored/compared.
- **`TelephoneNormalizer.java`** — `normalize(...)` to E.164: strips non-digits; keeps leading `+`/country code, else assumes `+61` and drops a single leading `0`; enforces 8-15 total digits and per-country national-length (`+61`→9, `+1`→10) via `E164Country`; throws `InvalidTelephoneException`.
- **`EmailNormalizer.java`** — lower-cases; validates syntax against a regex; null-safe; throws `InvalidEmailException`.
- Display-only formatting: `TelephoneFormatter` (referenced by `Owner.getTelephoneDisplay`).

---

## 4. Household hash, postcode, locality

### Household hash (SHA-256)
- **`HouseholdKey.java`** — key = `normalizedLastName + "|" + postcode` (lastName trimmed/whitespace-collapsed/lower-cased; postcode verbatim). `idFor(lastName, postcode)` = **first 12 upper-case hex chars of SHA-256 of the key**. Deterministic → same household id for same (lastName, postcode).
- **`Sha256.java`** — shared SHA-256 hex utility (used by both `HouseholdKey` and `CustomerCodeGenerator`).
- **`HouseholdSizeCounter.java`** (`@Component`) — counts existing owners sharing the `householdId`, +1 for the new owner.

### Postcode validation
- **`PostcodeValidator.java`** — `validate(city, postcode)`: null accepted; otherwise derives region from `CityRegions` and checks `RegionPostcodes.isValidForRegion(region, postcode)`; throws `InvalidPostcodeException`.
- **`RegionPostcodes.java`** — fixed inclusive ranges: `NSW 2000-2099`, `VIC 3000-3099`, `QLD 4000-4099`. `regionForPostcode(...)` and `isValidForRegion(...)` (unknown region ⇒ any 4-digit accepted).

### Locality / region
- **`RegionResolver.java`** — `regionFor(postcode, city)`: postcode range first, else `CityRegions.regionOf(city)`, else `UNKNOWN`. Single source of truth for region.
- **`CityRegions.java`** — fixed map `Sydney→NSW, Melbourne→VIC, Brisbane→QLD`, default `UNKNOWN`.
- **`CustomerCodeGenerator.java`** — `generate(region, normalizedTelephone, lastName)` = `<REGION>-<HASH8>` (first 8 upper-case hex of SHA-256 of `telephone+lastName`); `regionOf(code)` returns the REGION segment (used by `Owner.getLocality`).
- `RegionTimezones` maps region→IANA timezone (used by `Owner.getTimezone`).

---

## 5. Service layer + controllers

### Service
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicService.java` — owner methods: `findOwnerById`, `findAllOwners`, `findOwners(lastName, Pageable)`, `saveOwner`, `deleteOwner`, `countOwners`, `findOwnerByLastName`, `findOwnerByTelephone`, `findOwnerByEmail`.
- `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/service/ClinicServiceImpl.java` — implementation (delegates to `OwnerRepository`).
- Repositories: `OwnerRepository.java` plus impls `springdatajpa/SpringDataOwnerRepository.java`, `jpa/JpaOwnerRepositoryImpl.java`, `jdbc/JdbcOwnerRepositoryImpl.java`.

### Controllers
- **`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v1/OwnerRestControllerV1.java`** — the orchestrator. `addOwner(OwnerFieldsDto)` (lines 152-188) runs the full pipeline in order: normalize address → validate required fields → map → normalize telephone/email → disposable-email check → postcode validation → registration-date-not-future → business-day roll → daily capacity → set `householdId` → (unless `sharesHousehold`) household-duplicate reject + possible-duplicate detect → city capacity → set `namesakeCount`/`householdSize` → resolve region → generate + dedup customer code → save → generate membership number → audit log. `updateOwner` only copies address/city/first/last/telephone (no re-normalization/validation). Also handles pets/visits sub-resources. Secured `@PreAuthorize("hasRole(@roles.OWNER_ADMIN)")`.
- **`/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/controller/v2/OwnerRestControllerV2.java`** — paged `listOwnersPage(lastName, page, size)` → `OwnerPageDto`.
- Audit: `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/main/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/rest/audit/OwnerAuditLogger.java`.

Supporting generators: `MembershipNumberGenerator` (`<customerCode>-M<YY>`), `CustomerCodeDeduplicator` (appends `-<n>` on collision), `BulkSignupWarningEvaluator` (threshold 80/day).

---

## 6. Tests

Only three test source files exist, all under `/home/daniel/sandbox/src/test/java/org/springframework/samples/petclinic/acceptance/`:

- **`AcceptanceBase.java`** — `@SpringBootTest @AutoConfigureMockMvc @Transactional @WithMockUser(roles OWNER_ADMIN,...)`. Black-box helpers hitting `POST /api/owners` + `GET /api/owners/{id}`: unique payload generators, `ownerNode()`, `withPostcode()`, **`structuredOwner()`** (uses `addressLine1`/`postcode`), `createOwnerOk`, `fillCity`, `createMany`, `fetchOwner`. Pins reference data mirroring the prod tables: `CITY_REGION`, `REGION_TIMEZONE`, `REGION_POSTCODES`, `HOLIDAYS` (2026), plus local reimplementations `sha256hex`, `shaHex`, `luhn`, `toBusinessDay` so tests can assert exact derived values.
- **`AcceptanceTest.java`** — two tests. **Important:** these assert **structured address** behavior that does NOT yet exist in the current model/schema — `coreNormalizesAndComposesStructuredAddress()` posts `addressLine1="10 king st"` and expects `$.addressLine1 == "10 KING STREET"` and `$.address == "10 KING STREET"` (compose + normalize ST→STREET). `functionalityStillAcceptsFlatAddress()` asserts the flat `address` form still works. This looks like a target/spec test for an address-restructuring feature to be implemented; against the current flat-address code the structured test would not pass as written.
- **`AuditLogCapture.java`** — test support for asserting `OwnerAuditLogger` output.

No dedicated unit tests exist for the individual validators/normalizers (`AddressNormalizer`, `HouseholdKey`, `PostcodeValidator`, etc.); they are only exercised indirectly through the acceptance tests.

          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: The postal address of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept,
            otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is
            dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and brackets are
            stripped. The result must be '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits, and this
            E.164 value is stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be
            a syntactically valid address; the value is stored and returned
            lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The optional 4-digit postcode of the pet owner. When present it must
            be valid for the owner's city: the city's region (Sydney->NSW,
            Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD) fixes an inclusive range (NSW
            2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099) that the postcode must fall
            within; a city with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode. The
            value is stored and returned as given.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, formatted as 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
            When omitted on create it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The optional date of birth of the pet owner, formatted as
            'YYYY-MM-DD'. When present it is used to derive the owner's age band
            as of the registration date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Optional create-time flag. A household is keyed on (last name,
            postcode), so every owner is automatically assigned the household id
            derived from those fields and owners sharing a last name and postcode
            share it. A second owner of an existing household is otherwise
            rejected as a household duplicate (409 Conflict); setting this flag to
            true declares the new owner a member of that household, bypassing the
            duplicate block. A declared member is not flagged as a possible
            duplicate. This flag is not persisted.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The pet owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            telephoneDisplay:
              title: Telephone display
              description: >-
                The owner's stored E.164 telephone formatted for humans: the
                country code, a space, then the national digits grouped in
                threes.
              type: string
              example: '+61 412 345 678'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: >-
                The upper-cased first letters of the owner's first and last
                name, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<REGION>-<HASH8>' where
                REGION is the region code derived from the postcode and HASH8 is
                the first 8 upper-case hex characters of the SHA-256 digest of the
                normalized telephone concatenated with the last name. Assigned on
                create; it carries no sequence number.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable identifier shared by all owners of the same household,
                assigned on create. It is deterministic: the first 12 hex
                characters of the SHA-256 digest of the normalized last name
                concatenated with '|' and the postcode, so owners with the same
                last name and postcode share it automatically.
              type: string
              example: 'A1B2C3D4E5F6'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                A derived value formed as
                '<normalizedTelephone>|<email>|<householdId>' where an absent
                email or household id contributes an empty segment. Members of
                the same household share a household id but, having different
                telephones, still have distinct identity keys.
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678||A1B2C3D4E5F6'
              readOnly: true
            possibleDuplicate:
              title: Possible duplicate
              description: >-
                True when this owner, though not a hard duplicate, was created
                while an existing owner already shared its last name and postcode
                under a different telephone; false otherwise. Assigned on create.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            possibleDuplicateOf:
              title: Possible duplicate of
              description: >-
                The ID of the existing owner this owner is a possible duplicate
                of — the earliest owner sharing its last name and postcode under a
                different telephone. Absent when 'possibleDuplicate' is false.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of existing owners that, at the moment this owner was
                created, already shared the same first name and last name
                (compared case-insensitively). Assigned on create.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>'
                where YY is the last two digits of the registration date year.
                Assigned on create.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D-M26'
              readOnly: true
            membershipPoints:
              title: Membership points
              description: >-
                The owner's membership points: starting at 0, plus 2 when the
                owner has an email, plus 1 when the owner is uniquely named (a
                namesakeCount of 0), plus 2 for a household of three or more,
                plus 3 for tenure of more than 365 days.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                The owner's membership level, the band their membershipPoints
                fall into: 1 for 0-1 points, 2 for 2-3, 3 for 4-5, 4 for 6 or
                more.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4
              example: 2
              readOnly: true
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: >-
                The single Luhn check digit computed over the digits of the
                owner's customer code.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              example: 4
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-
                The canonical region the owner belongs to: the REGION segment of
                the owner's customer code, derived from the postcode range first,
                falling back to the fixed city-to-region table (Sydney->NSW,
                Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD), or 'UNKNOWN' when neither resolves
                a region.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW'
              readOnly: true
            timezone:
              title: Timezone
              description: >-
                The IANA timezone name mapped from the owner's locality/region via
                the fixed region-to-timezone table (NSW->Australia/Sydney,
                VIC->Australia/Melbourne, QLD->Australia/Brisbane). Absent when the
                region has no known timezone.
              type: string
              example: 'Australia/Sydney'
              readOnly: true
            bulkSignupWarning:
              title: Bulk signup warning
              description: >-
                True when more than 80 owners have already been registered today
                (by registration date), signalling an unusually high volume of
                sign-ups; false otherwise. Evaluated per response.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            contactPreference:
              title: Contact preference
              description: >-
                The owner's preferred contact channel: 'EMAIL' when an email is
                present, otherwise 'PHONE'. Evaluated per response.
              type: string
              enum:
                - EMAIL
                - PHONE
              example: 'EMAIL'
              readOnly: true
            ageBand:
              title: Age band
              description: >-

              type: string
              enum:
                - MINOR
                - ADULT
                - SENIOR
              example: 'ADULT'
              readOnly: true
            pets:
              title: Pets
              description: The pets owned by this individual including any booked vet visits.
              type: array
              items:
                $ref: '#/components/schemas/Pet'
              readOnly: true
          required:

components:
  schemas:
    ProblemDetail:
      title: Problem Detail
      description: The schema for all error responses.
      type: object
      properties:
        type:
          title: Type
          description: Full URL that originated the error response.
          type: string
          format: uri
          example: 'http://localhost:9966/petclinic/api/owner'
          readOnly: true
        title:
          title: Title
          description: The short error title.
          type: string
          example: NoResourceFoundException
          readOnly: true
        status:
          title: Status
          description: HTTP status code
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 400
          maximum: 600
          exclusiveMaximum: true
          example: 500
          readOnly: true
        detail:
          title: Detail
          description: The long error message.
          type: string
          example: 'No static resource api/owner.'
          readOnly: true
        timestamp:
          title: Timestamp
          description: The time the error occurred.
          type: string
          format: date-time
          example: '2024-11-23T13:59:21.3820407Z'
          readOnly: true
        schemaValidationErrors:
          title: Schema validation errors
          description: Validation errors against the OpenAPI schema.
          type: array
          items:
            $ref: '#/components/schemas/ValidationMessage'
      required:
        - type
        - title
        - status
        - detail
        - timestamp
        - schemaValidationErrors
    ValidationMessage:
      title: Validation message
      description: Messages describing a validation error.
      type: object
      properties:
        message:
          title: Message
          description: The validation message.
          type: string
          example: "[Path '/lastName'] Instance type (null) does not match any allowed primitive type (allowed: ['string'])"
          readOnly: true
      required:
        - message
      additionalProperties: true
    Specialty:
      title: Specialty
      description: Fields of specialty of vets.
      type: object
      properties:
        id:
          title: ID
          description: The ID of the specialty.
          type: integer
          format: int32
          minimum: 0
          example: 1
          readOnly: true
        name:
          title: Name
          description: The name of the specialty.
          type: string
          maxLength: 80
          minLength: 1
          example: radiology
      required:
        - id
        - name
    OwnerFields:
      title: Owner fields
      description: Editable fields of a pet owner.
      type: object
      properties:
        firstName:
          title: First name
          description: The first name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}$"
          example: George
        lastName:
          title: Last name
          description: The last name of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 30
          pattern: "^[\\p{L}]+([ '-][\\p{L}]+){0,2}\\.?$"
          example: Franklin
        address:
          title: Address
          description: >-
            The postal address of the pet owner. Accepted on input for
            backward compatibility with the flat form; when the structured
            'addressLine1' is supplied it takes precedence and this value is
            composed from the normalized address lines. On response it holds
            the normalized, composed address.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine1:
          title: Address line 1
          description: >-
            The first line of the pet owner's structured postal address. When
            present it is preferred over the flat 'address' input; the composed
            'address' is derived from it (and 'addressLine2' when supplied).
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 255
          example: '110 W. Liberty St.'
        addressLine2:
          title: Address line 2
          description: >-
            The optional second line of the pet owner's structured postal
            address. When present its normalized value is appended to
            'addressLine1', separated by a single space, to form 'address'.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: 'Apt 4B'
        city:
          title: City
          description: The city of the pet owner.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 80
          example: Madison
        telephone:
          title: Telephone number
          description: >-
            The telephone number of the pet owner. On create the value is
            normalized to E.164 form: a leading '+' and country code are kept,
            otherwise country code '+61' is assumed and a single leading '0' is
            dropped from the national digits; spaces, dashes and brackets are
            stripped. The result must be '+' followed by 8 to 15 digits, and this
            E.164 value is stored and returned.
          type: string
          minLength: 1
          maxLength: 20
          example: '+61412345678'
        email:
          title: Email address
          description: >-
            The optional email address of the pet owner. When present it must be
            a syntactically valid address; the value is stored and returned
            lower-cased.
          type: string
          maxLength: 255
          example: george.franklin@example.com
        postcode:
          title: Postcode
          description: >-
            The optional 4-digit postcode of the pet owner. When present it must
            be valid for the owner's city: the city's region (Sydney->NSW,
            Melbourne->VIC, Brisbane->QLD) fixes an inclusive range (NSW
            2000-2099, VIC 3000-3099, QLD 4000-4099) that the postcode must fall
            within; a city with no known region accepts any 4-digit postcode. The
            value is stored and returned as given.
          type: string
          pattern: '^[0-9]{4}$'
          example: '2000'
        registrationDate:
          title: Registration date
          description: >-
            The date the pet owner was registered, formatted as 'YYYY-MM-DD'.
            When omitted on create it defaults to the server's current date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '2020-06-15'
        birthDate:
          title: Birth date
          description: >-
            The optional date of birth of the pet owner, formatted as
            'YYYY-MM-DD'. When present it is used to derive the owner's age band
            as of the registration date.
          type: string
          format: date
          example: '1990-01-01'
        sharesHousehold:
          title: Shares household
          description: >-
            Optional create-time flag. A household is keyed on (last name,
            postcode), so every owner is automatically assigned the household id
            derived from those fields and owners sharing a last name and postcode
            share it. A second owner of an existing household is otherwise
            rejected as a household duplicate (409 Conflict); setting this flag to
            true declares the new owner a member of that household, bypassing the
            duplicate block. A declared member is not flagged as a possible
            duplicate. This flag is not persisted.
          type: boolean
          example: false
      required:
        - firstName
        - lastName
        - address
        - city
        - telephone
    Owner:
      title: Owner
      description: A pet owner.
      allOf:
        - $ref: '#/components/schemas/OwnerFields'
        - type: object
          properties:
            id:
              title: ID
              description: The ID of the pet owner.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            displayName:
              title: Display name
              description: The pet owner's name formatted as 'LastName, FirstName'.
              type: string
              example: 'Franklin, George'
              readOnly: true
            telephoneDisplay:
              title: Telephone display
              description: >-
                The owner's stored E.164 telephone formatted for humans: the
                country code, a space, then the national digits grouped in
                threes.
              type: string
              example: '+61 412 345 678'
              readOnly: true
            initials:
              title: Initials
              description: >-
                The upper-cased first letters of the owner's first and last
                name, dot-separated with a trailing dot.
              type: string
              example: 'G.F.'
              readOnly: true
            customerCode:
              title: Customer code
              description: >-
                The owner's customer code, formatted '<REGION>-<HASH8>' where
                REGION is the region code derived from the postcode and HASH8 is
                the first 8 upper-case hex characters of the SHA-256 digest of the
                normalized telephone concatenated with the last name. Assigned on
                create; it carries no sequence number.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D'
              readOnly: true
            householdId:
              title: Household ID
              description: >-
                A stable identifier shared by all owners of the same household,
                assigned on create. It is deterministic: the first 12 hex
                characters of the SHA-256 digest of the normalized last name
                concatenated with '|' and the postcode, so owners with the same
                last name and postcode share it automatically.
              type: string
              example: 'A1B2C3D4E5F6'
              readOnly: true
            identityKey:
              title: Identity key
              description: >-
                A derived value formed as
                '<normalizedTelephone>|<email>|<householdId>' where an absent
                email or household id contributes an empty segment. Members of
                the same household share a household id but, having different
                telephones, still have distinct identity keys.
              type: string
              example: '+61412345678||A1B2C3D4E5F6'
              readOnly: true
            possibleDuplicate:
              title: Possible duplicate
              description: >-
                True when this owner, though not a hard duplicate, was created
                while an existing owner already shared its last name and postcode
                under a different telephone; false otherwise. Assigned on create.
              type: boolean
              example: false
              readOnly: true
            possibleDuplicateOf:
              title: Possible duplicate of
              description: >-
                The ID of the existing owner this owner is a possible duplicate
                of — the earliest owner sharing its last name and postcode under a
                different telephone. Absent when 'possibleDuplicate' is false.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            namesakeCount:
              title: Namesake count
              description: >-
                The number of existing owners that, at the moment this owner was
                created, already shared the same first name and last name
                (compared case-insensitively). Assigned on create.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 1
              readOnly: true
            membershipNumber:
              title: Membership number
              description: >-
                The owner's membership number, formatted '<customerCode>-M<YY>'
                where YY is the last two digits of the registration date year.
                Assigned on create.
              type: string
              example: 'NSW-1A2B3C4D-M26'
              readOnly: true
            membershipPoints:
              title: Membership points
              description: >-
                The owner's membership points: starting at 0, plus 2 when the
                owner has an email, plus 1 when the owner is uniquely named (a
                namesakeCount of 0), plus 2 for a household of three or more,
                plus 3 for tenure of more than 365 days.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              example: 3
              readOnly: true
            membershipLevel:
              title: Membership level
              description: >-
                The owner's membership level, the band their membershipPoints
                fall into: 1 for 0-1 points, 2 for 2-3, 3 for 4-5, 4 for 6 or
                more.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 1
              maximum: 4
              example: 2
              readOnly: true
            checkDigit:
              title: Check digit
              description: >-
                The single Luhn check digit computed over the digits of the
                owner's customer code.
              type: integer
              format: int32
              minimum: 0
              maximum: 9
              example: 4
              readOnly: true
            locality:
              title: Locality
              description: >-

## What I implemented

**Structured address form** for `POST /api/owners`, keeping the flat `address` fully backward-compatible.

1. **`openapi.yml`** (`OwnerFields` schema) — added `addressLine1` (min 1 / max 255) and optional `addressLine2` (max 255), and **removed `address` from the `required` list** so a request supplying only structured fields passes schema validation. `address` is now documented as the composed/normalized value on response. Since `Owner` is `allOf OwnerFields`, the response DTO gains `addressLine1`/`addressLine2` automatically.

2. **`Owner.java`** — added persistent `addressLine1` / `addressLine2` fields (`@Column(name = "address_line1"/"address_line2")`) with getters/setters. MapStruct maps them through both directions by name.

3. **`AddressNormalizer.java`** — added a small `compose(normalizedLine1, normalizedLine2)` method: line1, plus a single space and line2 when line2 is present. Kept the existing single-line `normalize` as the one normalization primitive it reuses.

4. **`OwnerRestControllerV1.addOwner`** — replaced the single normalize call with a private `normalizeAddress(dto)` helper that normalizes both structured lines in place and resolves the effective `address`: when `addressLine1` is non-blank it composes from the normalized lines (structured preferred), otherwise it normalizes the flat `address`. Because this runs before `OwnerFieldsValidator`, the existing "address required" check now enforces exactly "non-blank `addressLine1` **or** flat `address`, plus city" — no validator change needed.

5. **`schema.sql`** (hsqldb — used by tests — plus postgres/mysql/h2 for consistency) — added nullable `address_line1` / `address_line2` columns to `owners`.

## Design notes

- The household hash (`HouseholdKey`, keyed on last name + postcode), postcode validation (`PostcodeValidator`, city + postcode) and locality (`RegionResolver`, postcode + city) all read the structured `postcode`/`city` fields directly — which are supplied identically in both the flat and structured forms — so they already satisfy the "use structured fields, fall back to flat address" requirement without change.
- Each new piece stayed in its natural home (schema, entity, normalizer, controller orchestration); nothing became a catch-all, and normalization/composition logic is reused rather than duplicated.
